build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player builds enclosures on a grid by fencing areas and assigning biome types. Animals are placed in enclosures. Enclosure biome must match animal habitat requirements or the animal becomes stressed. Score 0 if there is no enclosure building, if biomes do not exist, or if habitat matching has no effect.

Visitors enter through a gate, walk paths, view enclosures, and spend money on admission and amenities. Visitor count and happiness are tracked. More visitors means more revenue. Score 0 if visitors do not appear, if they generate no revenue, or if happiness is not tracked.

A money economy drives the zoo: admission and amenity sales generate income, animal purchases and staff salaries are expenses. A money counter is permanently visible. Score 0 if there is no money system or if everything is free.

Animal welfare is tracked per animal with a visible mood indicator. Welfare depends on enclosure size, biome match, and companion animals. Stressed animals are less attractive to visitors. Score 0 if animal welfare does not exist or if it has no gameplay effect.

The full loop connects: title -> new zoo -> build/manage/observe -> time advances (seasons) -> zoo thrives or fails -> result screen. The game shows seasonal summaries with visitor and financial stats. Score 0 if any transition is missing or if there is no time progression.
At least five animal species exist with different sprites, habitat requirements, popularity ratings, and costs. Score 0 if fewer than four species exist or if species are visually identical.

At least three biome types exist (savanna, arctic, jungle, aquatic) with visually distinct enclosure appearances. Different animals require different biomes. Score 0 if biomes do not exist or if all enclosures look identical.

Visitor amenities (food stalls, gift shops, rest areas) can be built and affect visitor happiness and spending. At least three amenity types exist. Score 0 if no amenities exist or if they have no effect.

Breeding is possible when compatible animals share a well-maintained enclosure. Baby animals increase visitor draw and can be kept or traded. Score 0 if breeding does not exist or if it has no gameplay effect.

Conservation goals provide bonus objectives (breed endangered species, maintain genetic diversity, reach welfare targets). Completing goals earns rewards or unlocks. Score 0 if no goals exist beyond profit.
The HUD shows money, visitor count, overall animal welfare, and current season in clear non-overlapping regions. Score 0 if money, visitors, or welfare is missing.

The zoo view clearly shows paths, enclosures with distinct biomes, animals inside enclosures, visitors walking, and amenities. The build menu and play area are separated. Score 0 if enclosures are indistinguishable or if animals are invisible.

Actions produce visible feedback: building shows structures appear, placing animals shows them in enclosures, visitors react to exhibits, welfare changes show mood indicators, and breeding shows baby animals. Score 0 if actions produce no observable change.

Overall art coherence: enclosures, animals, paths, visitors, amenities, and UI belong to a consistent bright, educational zoo visual language with lush natural tones. Score 0 if the screen mixes incompatible styles or reads as plain default plain grey. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

Animal sprites are real illustrated or pixel-art creatures with distinct species appearances. Visitors are character sprites, not dots. Score 0 if animals are plain colored shapes or if visitors are featureless.

Enclosures use real textured biome tiles (grass, snow, jungle foliage, water) with environmental detail. Paths and amenities have illustrated appearances. Score 0 if enclosures are flat colored areas.

HUD and UI use styled themed widgets with nature-park chrome: animal cards have illustrated frames, welfare indicators have themed icons, and menus have natural-material backgrounds. Score 0 if UI elements are unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults.

Animation and atmosphere: animals move and idle within enclosures, visitors walk and stop at exhibits, amenities show activity, and the zoo has ambient life (birds, rustling leaves, water features). Score 0 if all elements are static.
